title: Cross-platform command resolution without shell=true
context: On Windows, spawn(cmd, args, {shell: false}) fails for .cmd/.bat launchers like npx.cmd and npm.cmd — Node won't run them directly. This silently recorded exit_code: null on every Windows verification check, making contribution cards unactionable ('no independent command result'). Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Implement resolveSpawnCommand() that intelligently handles each case: npm/npx route to their underlying Node CLI scripts and spawn directly; other .cmd/.bat files route through cmd.exe with /d /s /c and pre-quoted args; real .exe/.com files spawn as-is; PATH search for ambiguous commands. Keeps shell: false as security boundary while making Windows command execution actually work.
consequences: Windows verification checks now record real exit codes instead of null
npm and npx work correctly on Windows without spawning a shell
Introduces Windows-specific command resolution logic (launcher shims, PATHEXT search, cmd.exe routing)
Adds structural abstraction (ResolvedSpawn interface) that could be reused for other cross-platform spawn calls
Failure to resolve now streams an error instead of being swallowed as null
alternatives_rejected: Use shell: true for Windows only — simpler but opens injection vectors and inconsistent shell parsing across platforms
Skip verification on Windows — leaves functionality broken
Pre-resolve and cache command paths — less flexible, harder to maintain
Accept null and special-case it downstream — leaves the root bug unfixed
